summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Genzao studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950 and trained under traditional teachers Jiangze Rinpoche in 1948 and Kalu Rinpoche.

Working in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies, Widengren studied at Stockholm University and Uppsala University, earning a doctorate under Henrik Samuel Nyberg. He was a professor at Uppsala (1940-1973) and served as president of the IAHR (~1960-1970).

Childs specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, where he studied under Tsetan Chonjore, and held posts at the Australian National University and Washington University in St. Louis (attested 2003-2005).

Barstow works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Hampshire College, Kathmandu University, and the University of Virginia (PhD), training also under Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche, and became assistant professor of religious studies at Oregon State University (~2013).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, Goble earned his MA at the University of Virginia and his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington. He served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Oklahoma (attested 2019).

Specializing in religious studies, Tibetology, and Indology, Samuel earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach, Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, and Peter J. Wilson. He held professorships at the University of Newcastle, Lancaster University, and Cardiff University.

Buddruss worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate under Paul Thieme at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1950-1954), studied at the University of Tübingen, and served as professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1963-1995).

A scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology, Bühler studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He held professorships at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai (1863-1880) and held the Sanskrit chair at the University of Vienna from 1880.
Working in philosophy and other fields, Lichtenberg studied at the University of Göttingen (~1763-1767) and later served on its faculty from circa 1770 to 1799.

A linguist who studied at Bonn and Berlin under Lassen, Ritschl, Schlegel, and Bopp, Curtius held professorships of classical philology at Charles University (1849-1854), Kiel University (1854-1862), and the University of Leipzig (1862-1885).
Working in Indology and other fields, Forster was educated at Saint Peter's School and held academic posts at Vilnius University (1784-1787) and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1788-1793).

A scholar of linguistics and other fields, Freytag studied at the University of Göttingen and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He served as professor of Oriental languages at the University of Bonn from 1819 to 1861.
Specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics, Grotefend was educated at the Lessing-Gymnasium and studied at the University of Göttingen (~1795-1797).

Specializing in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, Huth studied at the University of Leipzig (~1885-1889) and later held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1891-1906).
A scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology, Kaibel held academic posts at the universities of Rostock (~1879-1882), Greifswald (~1882-1883), Breslau (~1883-1886), and Göttingen (~1897-1901).

Active in linguistics and other fields, Dissen studied at the University of Göttingen (~1803-1807). He subsequently held posts at the University of Marburg (~1812-1813) and the University of Göttingen (~1813-1837).

Dursch specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tübingen and under Antoine-Léonard Chézy at the University of Paris (~1827-1829), later serving as a professor at Johann-Vanotti-Gymnasium Ehingen beginning in 1829.

An Indologist and linguist who also worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Morgenstierne studied at Oslo, Bonn, and Berlin, learning under Sten Konow, Heinrich Lüders, and Wilhelm Schulze. He held professorships at the University of Gothenburg (1930-1937) and Oslo (1937-1962).
Specializing in philosophy and other fields, Simmel studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1876-1881) and later held an academic post there from circa 1885 to 1914.

The philosopher Hegel studied at the Tübinger Stift, the University of Tübingen, and the University of Jena under Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling. He held positions at Jena (~1801-1807), Heidelberg University (~1816-1818), and Frederick William University Berlin (~1818-1831).
